text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 finished off the day's best levels on Friday, but at a sixth consecutive closing peak as bid speculation and stock shortages fuelled the financials to record levels. The leading stock index ended more than one percent or 50.5 points higher at 4,630.9, to chalk up a rise of 175.3 points this week.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended a dull session of bourse trade on Friday slightly higher, as many market players extended the Ascension Thursday holiday into a long weekend, lowering volumes appreciably. Firm Bunds, strong futures and an upbeat overnight close on Wall Street underpinned sentiment over the session and the DAX index, which measures bourse trade in 30 blue-chip stocks, ended up 10.43 points, at 3,562.41 points a gain of 102.04 from last Friday's close. In post-bourse trade the index fell 4.24 to 3,533.21.

PARIS - French shares closed lower on Friday, ignoring rises on Wall Street and fresh records in London, because of a weaker dollar and unease over a diminishing lead of the government in pre-election opinion polls. The French market was closed on Thursday when remarks by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan helped bonds and shares and it woke up to a dollar hurt by comments by Japan's "Mr Yen" Eisuke Sakakibara. The CAC-40 index closed down 9.40 points at 2633.91 and down 21.4 on the week.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended lower but kept above the psychologically important level of 5,000 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), while the shares of Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) and ABB Asea Brown Boveri posted strong gains. Weakness in index-heavyweights Roche and Novartis put pressure on the whole market, dealers said. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended up 0.54 points to 3,167.82 a gain of 40.35 on the week.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended lower in the Friday session, closing below the 20,000 threshold for the first time this week.

Brokers said profit-taking by both foreign and domestic institutional investors hit the major indices as the yen strengthened against the dollar. The 225-share Nikkei average fell 259.03 points to 19,802.78 but gained 288.03 from last weeks close.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks thundered to a record close on Friday, powered by a scramble for the market's bluest blue chips and interest in a surprising red-chip deal, brokers said. The index gained 190.5 points to end at a record closing high of 13,930.80 and up 849.1 on the week.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market topped off a record breaking week with a new record close on Friday aided by stronger metal prices which boosted the resource sector and sparked off active trade in market leader BHP. Banks also continued to rally. The All Ordinaries index ended 21.3 points up at 2,526.0, breaking the previous record close of 2,517.6 set on Wednesday and up 34.4 from last Friday.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares ended firm as bullion broke out of its recent tight range of $340-$344 per ounce, to bounce to its highest fix in five weeks. South African gold shares were seen stronger next week if the yellow metal held its gains. Industrial shares ended flat after starting firmer on Wall Street's overnight 50-point gain. Dealers said local institutions entered the market in the morning after a lengthy absence but pulled out by noon, leaving industrials seeking direction. All-shares ended up 16.5 points at 7,179.4 and up 30.4 on the week, golds gained 23.2 points to 1,237.6 points, up 56 from last week and industrials were 3.8 points higher at 8,501.2 points but down 37.3 from last Friday.
